# Agents SDK v1.0.0-alpha.1

This first preview from `feat/simple-codex` adds Codex as an opt-in model provider for the Python Agents SDK. The prebuilt `openai-agents` wheels (version `1.0.0a1`) are available exclusively through GitHub Releases.

## Highlights

- **Choose Codex per run.** Import `CodexProvider` from `agents.models.codex` and create `provider = CodexProvider()`. Pass `RunConfig(model_provider=provider)` to the Runner. Codex uses your saved login. For API key authentication, use `CodexProvider(api_key=...)`. The provider selects the model for agents that use a model name or the default model. [Run the same agent with either provider](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/models/codex.md#run-one-agent-with-either-provider)
- **Reuse Codex Core inside Python.** The wheel embeds unmodified Codex Core `rust-v0.166.0` through PyO3. Direct calls to Core eliminate `codex app-server` startup and JSON-RPC. Reuse the provider to share one `ThreadManager` across calls. Each call gets a fresh thread. Use an SDK session for history and close the provider with `await provider.aclose()` when you finish. [Thread lifetime and history](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/models/codex.md#streaming-history-and-cancellation) · [Codex source](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/6ff1e1ca3b30fc8b914720681fcf5fe62e95f856)
- **Use SDK tools and approvals.** Stream text, hand off to a specialist, pause for approval before a Python tool runs, and validate typed output. Native commands follow Codex's sandbox and approval settings. A native approval prompt ends the model call. [Execution and approvals](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/models/codex.md#configure-execution) · [Supported tools and model settings](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/models/codex.md#supported-features-and-limits)

## Install and try it

Activate a virtual environment with standard CPython 3.10–3.14. Copy the link for your platform and replace `WHEEL_URL` in the command below. Each link includes the SHA-256 digest that pip checks when it downloads the wheel. [Checksums for all four wheels](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.1/SHA256SUMS)

[Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.28+)](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.1/openai_agents-1.0.0a1-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl#sha256=bfc5db104b0bb36d7119c8fb3f1d2831b6b8b7d95b63b09b2162bb721433057d) · [Linux ARM64 (glibc 2.28+)](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.1/openai_agents-1.0.0a1-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl#sha256=8a776dccb6baa8c197c090305138818bb70411fa34706c128cca8e1acb080e15) · [macOS 11+ on Apple silicon](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.1/openai_agents-1.0.0a1-cp310-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl#sha256=19a49f51ff30a201252ab1059e7b3ca00ab2b53f9d935ae65c489a6ee3284eba) · [Windows x64](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.1/openai_agents-1.0.0a1-cp310-abi3-win_amd64.whl#sha256=4bd8f0910bc39ac0074663f1b6a19c6345ab221f1bddb6758e8ad4588a94efa8)

```sh
python -m pip install --only-binary=:all: "WHEEL_URL"
```

To try the wildlife example, check out `v1.0.0-alpha.1` and run the command below from the repository root with the wheel installed. If your only credential is a saved Codex login, set `OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_TRACING=1` in your shell first. [Wildlife example](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/examples/model_providers/codex_provider.py) · [Authentication](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/models/codex.md#authenticate)

```sh
python -I examples/model_providers/codex_provider.py --codex
```

## Fixed

- Automatic session compaction uses local conversation history for Codex, including after an approval pause. Compaction needs its own OpenAI client or credentials. [Session compaction](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/sessions/index.md#openai-responses-compaction-sessions)
- Saved sandbox manifests preserve inline binary files when you resume a run. If you share these manifests, upgrade all readers before saving non-UTF-8 content. Use `LocalFile` when older SDKs need to read the manifest. [Manifest compatibility](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/sandbox/guide.md#manifest)

## Moving from the harness preview

If you use `Agent.run()` or `Session.submit()` in `v0.24.0-alpha.8`, move execution to `Runner.run()` or `Runner.run_streamed()` and select `CodexProvider` in your run config. If you use `agents.classic`, import `Agent`, `Runner`, and `RunConfig` from `agents`. [Previous harness release](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/tag/v0.24.0-alpha.8) · [Runner example](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/models/codex.md#run-one-agent-with-either-provider)

Finish pending native runs and approvals in your alpha.8 environment. Its `SessionState` checkpoints use a different format from the Runner's `RunState`. Start a fresh SDK session for conversation history in alpha.1. [SDK sessions](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/sessions/index.md#quick-start)

## Release verification

The SDK suite passed on the merged `feat/simple-codex` commit. CI built all four wheels and tested fresh installs on CPython 3.10 and 3.14 on each platform. We verified all four downloads against `SHA256SUMS`. [Source `87e8f533`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/commit/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc) · [SDK tests](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/44792830595) · [Wheel builds and installation checks](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/44792830563)

We also ran the wildlife example with a live model and the Linux x86-64 wheel on CPython 3.12. The specialist identified an American bison from the photo, called the Python catalog tool, and returned a typed report with record ID `synthetic-bison-001`. [Example and assertions](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/examples/model_providers/codex_provider.py)

## [0.25.0](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/compare/v0.24.0...v0.25.0) (2026-11-17)

## Key Changes

Version 0.25.0 removes the beta Runloop sandbox provider and changes how Pydantic run contexts are checkpointed. Runloop users should preserve their workspace data before switching providers. Applications that share checkpoints across workers should upgrade readers first.

### Highlights:

- Migrate Runloop workloads to another supported sandbox provider, such as Modal, or remain on 0.24.0 while migrating. Provider-specific sessions and snapshots require a separate data migration.
- Resume nested agent-tool approvals with output guardrails using RunState schema `1.22`. Pydantic checkpoints now preserve default values and in-place edits. Use a custom serializer for process-local resources.
- `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` now defaults to `gpt-6-luna`. Set `model="gpt-4.1"` to keep the previous choice. Agent model settings also follow the selected model more closely. Native Chat Completions tool requests for `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-luna` default to non-reasoning mode when no effort is supplied.
- Runner handoffs can opt into recovery with `failure_error_function`. Omitting it preserves exception propagation. The demo REPL can now approve or reject individual tool calls.
- MCP v2 Streamable HTTP supports concurrent requests. MCP v1 retains serialized requests. Failed and incomplete Responses calls now retain provider-reported token usage.

releases.body:
# Agents SDK v0.24.0-alpha.8

## Highlights

- **Approve Python tool calls before they run.** Review the arguments and approve or reject the call. You can remember a decision for the rest of the Session. [Managed approval example](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/managed_approvals/README.md#inspect-and-decide)
- **Connect your own model client.** The native tool loop works with async Responses and Chat Completions clients, LiteLLM, AnyLLM, and custom adapters. [Application-owned model clients](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/models.md#use-an-application-owned-model-client)
- **Add Realtime voice to a Session.** Use a server WebSocket, connect a browser over WebRTC, or attach to an existing SIP call. [Realtime connection options](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/native_voice.md#choose-a-connection)
- **Resume more kinds of work.** Save supported pending tool requests and approvals. Request and token budgets keep the usage already spent when you restore a supported checkpoint. [Restore a checkpoint with a budget](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/budgeted-recovery.md)
- **Install on more Linux systems.** The preview adds an ARM64 wheel. Both Linux wheels support glibc 2.28 or newer. [Preview wheel platform requirements](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/.github/RELEASING.md#L44)

## Added

- Observe tool-search calls, tool-search results, and hosted MCP approval decisions through `ModelOutputItemCompleted`. Use `include_execution_details=True` to receive full items; receive summaries by default. [Live tool observations](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/packages/codex/src/_agents_codex/observation.py#L238-L267)
- Use native Session Realtime APIs from `agents.realtime.native`, including `RealtimeAgentConfig(is_tool_enabled=...)`. Keep retained Classic/v0 Realtime imports under `agents.realtime`. [Native voice](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/native_voice.md#choose-a-connection) · [Classic imports](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/CLASSIC.md#compatible-voice-and-realtime-imports)
- Handle managed function approvals with `FunctionToolApprovalRequest` and `FunctionToolApprovalDecision`. Set `run_input_policy_before_approval=True` to run the input policy before the approval predicate as well as before execution. Return `FinishTurn(output)` from `tool_batch_completion` to propose a final value with output validation and completion checks. [Managed approvals](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/managed_approvals/README.md#inspect-and-decide) · [Finish a tool batch](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/outputs.md#finish-after-a-tool-batch)
- Create a remote conversation only when needed with `ConversationsHistory.ensure_conversation_id()`. Preserve a checked history prefix with `Session.replace_history_suffix(keep_prefix_count=...)`, and append staged checkpoint input with `SessionState.with_appended_pending_input()`. Read Unix milliseconds from `StoredTurn.started_at_ms` and `completed_at_ms`. [History APIs](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/reference.md#history-and-storage-apis) · [History edits](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/state.md#read-and-edit-original-history)
- Use `SQLAlchemySQLiteSessionStore` for an application-owned synchronous SQLite engine, and `ResponsesSocketFactoryOptions` for resolved WebSocket connection parameters. Read received logprob data through `TextLogprobsFact`, `TokenLogprob`, `TokenLogprobAlternative`, and `MalformedLogprobsFact`, with unchanged serialized record kinds. Import `ModelRunOwner` from `agents.models` and `ApplicationToolOutput` from `agents.state`. [SQLite storage](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/state.md#sqlalchemy-sqlite-storage) · [Model ownership and socket options](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/reference.md#model-run-ownership-and-websocket-options) · [Logprob facts](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/streaming.md#inspect-provider-logprobs)
- Group prompt-cache routing for fresh Sessions with an explicit `TraceOptions.group_id`. Keep the saved cache key when restoring a Session. Set a borrowed model adapter's `prompt_cache_key` to override only that adapter's outgoing key. Treat routing as affinity without a guaranteed cache hit. [Prompt-cache routing](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/observability.md#prompt-cache-routing-for-fresh-sessions)
- Route work through native handoffs or call a specialist with `Agent.as_tool()`. Add input and output guardrails, or use `Agent.decide()` for a separate typed decision with explicit input. [Handoffs](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/sessions.md#hand-off-the-conversation-to-another-agent) · [Typed decisions](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/decisions-guide.md)
- Use standalone Python function tools and select MCP tools by alias. Defer eligible tool schemas with `ToolSearch`. Function tools also support strict schemas, output schemas, and an option to ignore extra arguments. [Python tool declarations](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/tools.md#python-functions) · [Tool schema discovery](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/tools.md#discover-tool-schemas)
- Use Redis, MongoDB, SQLAlchemy, or a Dapr Redis state component to store supported root conversations through `CustomStorage`. Compatible Responses providers also support provider-managed conversation history. [Application-owned storage](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/state.md#store-history-in-an-application-backend)
- Use ordinary manual `FunctionTool` requests and preapproved `HttpMCP` tools with `CustomStorage`. Suspend a supported manual request and restore into independent memory. To continue through the original backend, use an unchanged checkpoint with one unresolved ordinary manual call. Keep managed function approvals, pending MCP requests, and staged input outside that same-backend restore path. [CustomStorage support and checkpoint limits](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/state.md#store-history-in-an-application-backend)
- Open read-only execution environments, supply skills, or implement command and patch tools with application callbacks. Callbacks run with the application's permissions. [Read-only workspaces](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/execution.md#inspect-a-read-only-workspace) · [Native skills](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/execution.md#supply-native-skills)
- Set per-request model options for sampling, retries, deadlines, and prompt caching. Request produced items and history from one-shot runs, or opt in to provider reasoning summaries and tool-argument deltas. [Model request controls](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/models.md#model-request-controls) · [Streaming and retained history](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/streaming.md#inspect-observations-and-retained-history)

## Changed

- Native streaming HTTP can negotiate HTTP/2. Buffered Responses continue to use HTTP/1.1.
- Set `NativeProvider(tool_output_token_limit=...)` to adjust the approximate tool-result budget for model context. Leave it unset to use the model's default. The setting is separate from the final answer limit. [Tool output limit reference](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/packages/codex/src/_agents_codex/agent.py#L488-L497)

## Fixed

- Reject invalid web-starter request bodies and prompts before admitting work. Reject deeply nested JSON, non-object bodies, and text without valid UTF-8 encoding. [Web-starter request validation](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/web_starter/app.py#L433-L474)
- Wait for confirmed remote command exit during cancellation. Report a failure when the executor acknowledges a stop without confirming exit.
- Preserve the backing store's configured history limit when a Classic compaction wrapper has no explicit settings. Explicit wrapper and per-run limits still take precedence.
- Strict Python tools return a retryable error to the model when the original arguments fail validation, before approval or callback execution. A corrected call still goes through approval when required. [Function argument validation reference](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/packages/codex/src/_agents_codex/_function_tools.py#L1390-L1404)
- Preserve completed tool results during supported checkpoint restores. Report uncertain calls for reconciliation before reopening local profiles with interrupted child work. [Recover after an interruption](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/state.md#recover-after-interruption)
- Preserve accepted model settings and history across supported handoffs and retries. Improve provider error reporting so applications can see where a request failed. [Inspect provider response attempts](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/streaming.md#inspect-response-attempts)
- Harden protection for native workspace metadata and credential files. Reduce startup work for simple runs and reuse eligible HTTP connections.

## Upgrading from 0.24.0-alpha.7

- Use the alpha.8 wheel for the features in these notes. Some linked guides still refer to development builds. If an example needs files from the repository, use the revision linked in these notes. Alpha.7 does not accept newer keywords such as `strict` on `function_tool` or `model_backend` on `NativeProvider`.
- For Linux local execution, install `bubblewrap` with a compatible `bwrap` in `/usr/bin` or `/bin` and allow sandbox namespace creation. For a Linux Docker executor, supply `bwrap` in the container image or executor bundle. [Linux executor setup](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/execution.md#local-execution)
- **Back up your saved state before upgrading.** Alpha.7 supports budgets for live runs. Alpha.8 adds checkpointing for supported pending runs with request or token budgets. The checkpoint saves the requests or tokens already used so they still count after restore. Alpha.7 rejects this new format because it cannot enforce the saved budget. We verified that both versions can reopen idle checkpoints, checkpoints waiting for a manual Python tool reply, and closed `LocalStorage` profiles on Linux x86-64. These checks used matching app settings and features available in both versions. If alpha.7 cannot reopen your saved state after rollback, restore your pre-upgrade backup. [Resume a budgeted checkpoint](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/budgeted-recovery.md) · [Checkpoint restore setup](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/state.md#supply-restore-configuration) · [Reopen a local profile](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/state.md#reopen-a-conversation-from-local-storage)
- Replace bare `"*"` entries in network domain rules with exact hosts or scoped patterns such as `"*.example.org"`. To allow outbound public hosts, use `NetworkPolicy.allow_all()`. On Linux, this also requires `allow_all_unix_sockets=True` and an executor isolated from host services and other jobs. Explicit network policies remain unsupported on Windows. [Network policy and platform limits](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/execution.md#network-and-local-socket-access)
- If you relied on a saved Codex login to enable ChatGPT Apps tools, add the existing `ChatGPTAppsMCP` declaration to the Agent's tools. Supply the provisioned Apps token, its account ID, and the tool names you want to expose. A saved Codex login now supplies model authentication only. [ChatGPT Apps setup](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/mcp.md#connect-personal-chatgpt-apps)
- If your code reads `session.items()`, count each execution once. Provider `function_call` and `function_call_output` rows can accompany a typed record for the same execution. Match native `thread_id`, `turn_id`, and `call_id` rather than counting rows or relying on a history cursor's `id`. Recheck saved-history readers and analytics before upgrading. [Execution history](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/streaming.md#inspect-completed-execution)
- If you use Classic `WorkspaceJsonlSink`, choose a log budget before upgrading. Its default is now 8 MiB. Exceeding the existing-file or pending-buffer budget drops pending events and permanently stops that sink; rebinding does not restart it. Create a new sink for a new outbox or a larger finite `max_bytes`, or use `JsonlOutboxSink` or `HttpProxySink` outside the workspace for long-lived logs. Use `max_bytes=None` only for trusted workloads that need unlimited reads. The sink does not rotate or truncate logs. [Workspace sink limits](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/src/agents/classic/sandbox/session/sinks.py#L143-L186)
- If you use the `classic-blaxel` extra and pin Blaxel, update the pin to `0.2.51` or newer. Test saved sandbox restoration with your current network and port settings. Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Modal, and Vercel can now reject saved settings that conflict with the current policy. Create a fresh sandbox with the required settings instead of relaxing the policy to reuse old state. # Agents SDK v0.24.0-alpha.7

## Highlights

- **Use Classic workflows alongside native execution.** Import the retained v0 runtime through `agents.classic`. This alpha also changes executor write defaults; review the upgrade actions before opening existing environments.
- **Keep conversations in your own storage.** Add durable root Sessions with `CustomStorage`, and reconcile uncertain tool effects before resuming work.
- **Add voice and hosted tools to native agents.** Connect speech workflows to a Session, or use `FileSearch`, `CodeInterpreter`, and `ImageGeneration` through compatible Responses providers.
- **Control context, completion, and usage.** Transform model input, retain selected context during compaction, review proposed answers, and limit observed root usage.

## Upgrading from 0.24.0-alpha.6

- **Review Environment write policies.** New Environments default to `write_policy="strict"`, which requires a compatible Linux or macOS executor. The working directory remains writable; use `writable_roots` for additional directories. To retain the previous remote policy, including on Windows executors, set `write_policy="legacy"` and leave `writable_roots=None`. Local execution requires strict mode. When restoring legacy remote checkpoints or profiles, select legacy explicitly; reopening does not upgrade their policy. See the [executor policy and restore rules](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/4c1190046163c09e4f67ab7254f22bea60b14894/docs/sdk/state.md#restore-executor-policy).
- **Check implicit reasoning settings.** The bundled model catalog changes the default reasoning effort from `low` to `medium` for `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, and `gpt-5.6-sol`. Set `model_settings={"reasoning_effort": "low"}` explicitly if you need the previous effort. This describes bundled metadata; an explicit setting or provider model metadata can select another value. (#5517)
- **Rename MCP approval modes.** Replace `approval_mode="auto"` with `"native"`, and `"approve"` with `"preapproved"`. The old values are rejected; the new names preserve their respective approval behavior.
- **Update child step callbacks.** `NativeAgents.before_step` now receives one `ChildStepContext`, with `context`, `child`, and `step_index`, instead of separate child and step-index arguments. Root `before_step` callbacks keep their existing signature.
- **Handle MCP forms and URLs separately.** `ElicitationRequest` is now the union `FormRequest | UrlRequest`. Use `FormRequest.reply()` or `respond()` for forms; use `UrlRequest.reply_url_accept()` or `accept_url()` for URL consent.

## Added

- **Application-owned conversation storage.** `SessionStore`, `SQLiteSessionStore`, and `CustomStorage` persist root history and automatic Python tool results. This initial profile excludes native tools, Environments, children, planning tools, generated-code execution, manual tools, and portable checkpoints. `SQLiteSessionStore` requires one host and a local POSIX filesystem. Both local profiles and custom stores can report uncertain root calls for explicit reconciliation; neither automatically replays those effects. (#5514, #5502)
- **Provider-hosted tools and storage.** Add `FileSearch`, `CodeInterpreter`, and `ImageGeneration`, Code Interpreter caller policies, and provider-managed storage. Hosted tools require an API-key provider and a compatible standard Responses model; they exclude Responses Lite and Codex login. Hosted web search adds domain and location controls and retains citations. (#5576, [hosted-tool guide](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/4c1190046163c09e4f67ab7254f22bea60b14894/docs/sdk/tools.md#provider-hosted-tools))
- **Context and completion hooks.** `Agent.transform_context` changes sampled input without changing stored history. `before_compact` and selected-item retention control compaction. `before_complete` can accept, return `ContinueTurn`, or stop a proposed answer; rejected text may already have streamed and remains in history. Advanced `prepare_request` editing supports a restricted HTTP profile. See the [hook contracts and limits](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/4c1190046163c09e4f67ab7254f22bea60b14894/docs/sdk/configuration.md#choose-a-model-context-hook).
- **Observed usage budgets.** `RunBudget` limits root request admissions, reported tokens, or estimated cost before the next request. An admitted request can exceed a limit. Children are excluded; missing usage stops further admission by default. Active budgeted operations cannot use portable checkpoints. (#5555)
- **MCP resources, prompts, and reconnection.** Use `Session.list_mcp_resources()`, `list_mcp_resource_templates()`, `read_mcp_resource()`, `list_mcp_prompts()`, and `get_mcp_prompt()` with a selected HTTP or stdio server while the Session is idle. Retrieved data does not enter model context automatically. Scoped tool selection and explicit reconnection preserve control over admitted tools without replaying uncertain calls. (#5597, #5604, #5556)
- **Local execution and project search.** `Environment.local()` runs supported executor tools locally. On Linux, `LocalStorageMount(source=path)` grants read-only access to an existing canonical directory; source and destination must match. `project_glob` and `project_grep` search beneath the Environment's fixed working directory without granting command execution. (#5501, #5575, #5574)
- **Integration and supervision.** Add native A2A client and server adapters through the `a2a` extra, explicit `TraceContext`, workflow tracing controls, API-key rate-limit snapshots, turn receipts, exact-turn steering, and attention waits. Classic integrations use the `classic` and `classic-*` extras; Classic and native objects and checkpoints remain separate.
- **Speech with native history and policies.** `agents.voice.NativeSessionVoiceWorkflow` uses a caller-owned text-output Session with the speech pipeline. It speaks accepted final text after completion review and output validation. The application handles interactions and Session lifetime. Install the `voice` extra; Realtime agents remain under `agents.classic.realtime`. (#5596)

## Changed

- **Choose function-tool timeout handling.** `timeout_behavior="error_as_result"` returns a timeout error to the model, with optional `timeout_error_function` formatting. Raising remains the default. (#5605)
- **Optional buffered Responses.** `NativeProvider(response_mode="buffered")` reads each complete HTTP JSON response before emitting model output. Select a standard Responses model explicitly; the default model uses Responses Lite. Buffered mode requires API-key authentication and excludes WebSockets, native children, and Codex login. Streaming remains the default. (#5589)
- **Experimental saved-login reuse.** `NativeProvider(auth=CodexLogin())` can use a saved Codex login over HTTP. Omit `api_key` and `base_url`. This experimental feature may change or be removed; see the [authentication guidance and limits](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/4c1190046163c09e4f67ab7254f22bea60b14894/docs/sdk/configuration.md#reuse-a-codex-login-experimental).

## Fixed

- Keep Classic mount credential files private during creation and replacement, and bound Classic sandbox archive extraction.
- Stop deferred work and automatic compaction after cancellation. Retain cleanup owners so callers can retry unfinished release of resources without repeating reconciliation or tool effects.
- Stop sampling retries after terminal provider authentication failures. Report typed output-failure reasons and captured context limits, and preserve cache-write token counts.
- Retain provider response observations and execution details under their configured policies. Reduce native startup and event-reading overhead.

## Release verification

Source: [`c27b24cc6c4fa7e89ab54fa9f795ef4f2d4d5fb9`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/commit/c27b24cc6c4fa7e89ab54fa9f795ef4f2d4d5fb9).

# Install the preview

Use standard CPython 3.10–3.14 in a virtual environment. These wheels include the native runtime; no Rust toolchain or source build is needed. This preview is distributed through GitHub Releases, not PyPI.

Run the command for your platform:

**Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.39 or newer)**

```sh
python -m pip install "https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v0.24.0-alpha.6/openai_agents-0.24.0a6-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_39_x86_64.whl"
```

**macOS 11 or newer on Apple Silicon**

```sh
python -m pip install "https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v0.24.0-alpha.6/openai_agents-0.24.0a6-cp310-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl"
```

**Windows x64**

```powershell
python -m pip install "https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v0.24.0-alpha.6/openai_agents-0.24.0a6-cp310-abi3-win_amd64.whl"
```

Wheels are not provided for Intel Macs, ARM Linux, ARM Windows, Alpine/musl, PyPy or free-threaded Python. The `cp310-abi3` filenames also support standard CPython 3.11–3.14.

Check the installed version and native module:

```sh
python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; import agents._native; print(version('openai-agents'))"
```

Expect `0.24.0-alpha.6` or its equivalent Python packaging spelling, `0.24.0a6`. `SHA256SUMS` contains checksums for all three wheels.

# Release notes

Changes since `0.24.0-alpha.5`. This preview expands conversation control, state recovery, and tool policies, and includes public API changes.

### Added

- Control submitted work through a captured `Turn`, with `get_result()`, passive `events()`, manual request handling, steering, and cancellation. Queue prompts with `Session.submit(..., if_busy="queue")`, or steer the active Turn with `if_busy="steer"`.
- Add `LocalStorage` to reopen conversations from a local profile, and extend portable `SessionState` capture and recovery. Add idle forks, caller-supplied compaction summaries, and checks for feature support and checkpoint readiness. `LocalStorage` profiles cannot export portable checkpoints.
- Add `NativeOutput` for native strict output and `PromptedOutput` for JSON validated in Python. Optional `max_retries` performs bounded corrections without tools or replaying the task. `LocalStorage` requires `max_retries=0`.
- Handle live manual tool requests and resume supported pending requests from checkpoints. Add experimental external-job recovery through `agents.experimental.deferred` and an optional MCP Tasks adapter.
- Select tools for each submission or model step within the Session's opening permissions. Add native web search, native child checklists, and native goals for local-storage Sessions.
- Validate Python tool return annotations and add tool policies for inspecting arguments and results. Extend native MCP support with argument replacement, result transforms, and application-managed form and URL interactions over supported HTTP, stdio, and model WebSocket paths.
- Add `NetworkPolicy` for native commands on supported Linux and macOS executors, subject to each platform's network and Unix socket limits. Manage remote executor lifetimes through an `Environment` supplied when opening a Session or running an Agent.
- Enable native child approvals and form requests with `NativeAgents(interactions=True)`. Children continue to share the Session's tools and application context.
- Configure native OpenTelemetry export and inspect typed observations. `NativeError` now exposes available provider status codes, error codes, request IDs, and failure categories.
- Test real SDK sessions and Python tools against local scripted responses with `agents.testing.ScriptedResponses`, without a live model or API key.

### API changes

- Use `Agent.run()` or `Agent.run_sync()` for one-shot calls; the redundant `Runner` aliases have been removed.
- Replace `Turn.wait()` and `Session.wait()` with `Turn.get_result()` on the captured Turn.
- Replace `Session.interrupt()` with `Turn.cancel()` for one root Turn or `Session.cancel_all()` for the whole Session.
- Rename `Subagent.submit()` to `Subagent.start()`. Unify Python callbacks and manual tools under `FunctionTool`; remove the separate `ManualTool` declaration.
- Agent declarations are immutable. Create a new Agent to change defaults, use `with_output_type()` for an output-type variant, or use supported idle Session updates for an open conversation.
- Tool selection and Session updates cannot expand the permissions captured when the Session opened. Restored Sessions use current application tools, credentials, and policies.

### Fixed

- Keep each captured Turn's result stable across accepted steering, native continuations, and later submissions. Preserve one-shot manual checkpoints, matching interaction replies, and output-repair state across supported save and restore boundaries.
- Improve native child cancellation and Session cleanup. Stop native work when result policies expire, and preserve policy failure reasons when reporting root and child results.
- Reject malformed Python tool result envelopes and preserve server errors through MCP result transforms. Support nested OpenAI extension forms and HTTP telemetry export with client certificates.

### Documentation and examples

- Move the preview source to the public repository. Refocus installation guidance on prebuilt wheels and move SDK build instructions to `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- Add examples for browser applications, AG-UI streaming, deferred jobs, evaluation, observability, and common application tasks. Remove migration guides from the preview documentation.

# Build and installation checks

Source: [2808233a56c32c9d7bb8b4f3bc739fe86e5fc282](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/commit/2808233a56c32c9d7bb8b4f3bc739fe86e5fc282). Wheels come from the successful [Tests run](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/actions/runs/41606126874).

## Key Changes

0.24.0 adds run-wide function error formatting and MCP discovery annotations, and improves recovery, sandbox safety, and tracing. This minor release includes compatibility changes for custom error callbacks and some saved agent graphs. Review the first two highlights before upgrading.

### Highlights:

- **Update custom error formatters.** `RunConfig.tool_error_formatter` can receive `kind="tool_exception"` and an optional `error`. Handle the new kind or return `None` to retain the default message. Explicit per-tool handlers keep precedence; unconfigured defaults stay unchanged.

## Key Changes

This minor release does **not** introduce a breaking change. The minor version bump reflects a significant new OpenAI Responses feature area: Programmatic Tool Calling.

### Highlights:

-   Added `agents.tool.ProgrammaticToolCallingTool`, which lets supported OpenAI Responses models generate JavaScript to coordinate eligible tools. It supports per-tool `allowed_callers`, structured function-tool outputs, and integration with Runner streaming, guardrails, approvals, sessions, and `RunState`. See [Programmatic Tool Calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling) for setup and constraints.
-   Added the public `agents.decorators` module and the shorter `@tool` alias alongside the existing function and guardrail decorators. Function tools now also support async callable objects.
-   SDK configuration now consistently accepts either typed settings objects or dictionaries across agents, runs, models, sessions, sandboxes, and voice pipelines, with validation for unknown settings.
-   Hardened error and diagnostic logging across models, tools, MCP, Realtime, sessions, sandboxes, and tracing to avoid exposing raw sensitive payloads while preserving useful debugging context.
-   Improved AnyLLM, LiteLLM, and Chat Completions compatibility, preserved session history across model retries, and added retries for WebSocket overloads that occur before a response starts.
-   Added `VercelCloudBucketMountStrategy`. Mounted sessions exclude bucket contents from workspace persistence and intentionally do not support dynamic mount changes or session resume.

## What's Changed

* feat: add Programmatic Tool Calling support by @seratch in https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/3833

## Key Changes

### RealtimeAgent's default is now gpt-realtime-2

Since this version, the default model for RealtimeAgents is gpt-realtime-2: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-realtime-2

### Sandbox local source materialization change

In this version, sandbox local source materialization keeps `LocalFile.src` and `LocalDir.src` within the materialization `base_dir` unless the source path is covered by `Manifest.extra_path_grants`. The `base_dir` is the SDK process current working directory when the manifest is applied; relative local sources are resolved from that directory, while absolute local sources must already be inside it or under an explicit grant. This closes a local artifact boundary issue, but it can affect applications that intentionally copy trusted host files or directories from outside that base directory into a sandbox workspace.Expand commentComment on line R24Resolved

To migrate, grant trusted host roots at the manifest level with `SandboxPathGrant`, preferably as read-only when the sandbox only needs to read those files:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from agents.sandbox import Manifest, SandboxPathGrant
from agents.sandbox.entries import Dir, LocalDir

# This is an absolute host path outside the SDK process base_dir.
TRUSTED_DOCS_ROOT = Path("/opt/my-app/docs")

manifest = Manifest(
    extra_path_grants=(
        # This host root is outside the SDK process base_dir, so the manifest must grant it.
        SandboxPathGrant(path=str(TRUSTED_DOCS_ROOT), read_only=True),
    ),
    entries={
        # No grant is needed for local sources that stay under the SDK process base_dir.
        "fixtures": LocalDir(src=Path("fixtures"), description="Local test fixtures."),
        # This entry reads from the granted host root and copies it into the sandbox workspace.
        "docs": LocalDir(src=TRUSTED_DOCS_ROOT, description="Trusted local documents."),
        # Dir creates a sandbox workspace directory; it does not read from the host filesystem.
        "output": Dir(description="Generated artifacts."),
    },
)
```

Treat `extra_path_grants` as trusted application configuration. Do not populate grants from model output or other untrusted manifest input unless your application has already approved those host paths.

## Key Changes

### Default model change

In this version, the SDK default model is now `gpt-5.4-mini` instead of `gpt-4.1`. This could affect agents and runs that do not explicitly set a model. Because the new default is a GPT-5 model, implicit default model settings now include GPT-5 defaults such as `reasoning.effort="none"` and `verbosity="low"`.

The new default model should work better for most use cases (see the report at https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/3147), but if you need to keep the previous default model behavior for some reasons, set a model explicitly on the agent or run config like `Agent(name="Assistant", model="gpt-4.1")`, or set the `OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL` environment variable.

### Disable max_turns detection

This version adds a new option `max_turns=None` to disable the Agents SDK run turn limit while preserving the existing default of `DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS` (`10`) when `max_turns` is omitted.

### Tool execution concurrency

This version adds a new SDK-side runtime configuration for local function tool execution concurrency: `ToolExecutionConfig(max_function_tool_concurrency=...)` on `RunConfig`, preserves default behavior when unset. The change keeps provider-side `ModelSettings.parallel_tool_calls` separate from SDK-side local execution scheduling.

### Server-prefixed MCP tool naming

This version adds a new option `include_server_in_tool_names` to MCPConfig. When it is set to True, the SDK includes the MCP server name in the tool name to prevent tool name conflicts with other MCP servers.

```python
agent = Agent(
    name="Assistant",
    mcp_servers=[my_mcp_server],
    mcp_config={"include_server_in_tool_names": True},
)
```

## Key Changes

### Better model refusal handling

In this version, model refusals are now surfaced explicitly as `ModelRefusalError` instead of being treated as empty text output or, for structured outputs, causing the run loop to retry until `MaxTurnsExceeded`.

This affects code that previously expected a refusal-only model response to complete with `final_output == ""`. To handle refusals without raising, provide a `model_refusal` run error handler:

```python
result = Runner.run_sync(
    agent,
    input,
    error_handlers={"model_refusal": lambda data: data.error.refusal},
)
```

For structured-output agents, the handler can return a value matching the agent's output schema, and the SDK will validate it like other run error handler final outputs.

releases.body:
## What's Changed

### Sandbox Agents

This release adds **Sandbox Agents**, a beta SDK surface for running agents with a persistent, isolated workspace. Sandbox agents keep the normal `Agent` and `Runner` flow, but add workspace manifests, sandbox-native capabilities, sandbox clients, snapshots, and resume support so agents can work over real files, run commands, edit repositories, generate artifacts, and continue work across runs.

Key pieces:

- `SandboxAgent`: an `Agent` with sandbox defaults such as `default_manifest`, sandbox instructions, capabilities, and `run_as`.
- `Manifest`: a fresh-workspace contract for files, directories, local files, local directories, Git repos, environment, users, groups, and mounts.
- `SandboxRunConfig`: per-run sandbox wiring for client creation, live session injection, serialized session resume, manifest overrides, snapshots, and materialization concurrency limits.
- Built-in capabilities for shell access, filesystem editing and image inspection, skills, memory, and compaction.
- Workspace snapshots and serialized sandbox session state for reconnecting to existing work or seeding a fresh sandbox from saved contents.

### Sandbox clients and hosted providers

Sandbox agents now support local, containerized, and hosted execution backends:

- `UnixLocalSandboxClient` for fast local development.
- `DockerSandboxClient` for container isolation and image parity.
- Hosted sandbox clients for Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Modal, Runloop, and Vercel through optional extras.

The release also adds provider-specific examples and mount strategies for common storage backends, including S3, Cloudflare R2, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, and S3 Files where supported by the selected backend.

### Sandbox memory

Adds a sandbox memory capability that lets future sandbox-agent runs learn from prior runs. Memory stores extracted lessons in the sandbox workspace, injects a concise summary into later runs, and uses progressive disclosure so agents can search deeper rollout summaries only when useful.

Memory supports:

- Read-only or generate-only modes.
- Live updates when the agent discovers stale memory.
- Multi-turn grouping through `conversation_id`, SDK `Session`, `RunConfig.group_id`, or generated run IDs.
- Separate memory layouts for isolating memory across agents or workflows.
- S3-backed examples for persisted memory across runs.

### Workspace mounts, snapshots, and resume

This release adds a full workspace entry and mount model for sandbox sessions:

- Local files and directories.
- Synthetic files and directories.
- Git repository entries.
- Remote storage mounts for S3, R2, GCS, Azure Blob Storage, and S3 Files.
- Provider-specific mount strategies across Docker, Modal, Cloudflare, Blaxel, Daytona, E2B, and Runloop.
- Portable snapshots with path normalization, symlink preservation, mount-safe snapshotting, and remote snapshot support.
- Resume paths through runner-managed `RunState`, explicit `SandboxSessionState`, or saved snapshots.

### Examples and tutorials

Adds a large `examples/sandbox/` suite covering:

- Local Unix and Docker sandbox runners.
- Docker mount smoke tests for S3, GCS, Azure Blob Storage, and S3 Files.
- Sandbox coding tasks with skills.
- Sandbox agents as tools and handoff patterns.
- Memory examples, including multi-agent/multi-turn memory and S3-backed memory.
- Tax-prep and healthcare-support workflows.
- Dataroom QA and metric extraction tutorials.
- Repository code review tutorial.
- Vision website clone tutorial.
- Provider examples for Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Modal, Runloop, Temporal, and Vercel.

### Runtime, tracing, and model plumbing

The release includes the runtime plumbing needed to make sandbox agents work naturally inside the existing SDK:

- Runner-managed sandbox preparation, capability binding, session lifecycle, state serialization, and resume behavior.
- Sandbox-aware `RunState` serialization.
- Unified sandbox tracing with SDK spans.
- Token usage on tracing spans.
- Runner-managed prompt cache key defaults.
- OpenAI agent registration and harness ID configuration.
- Safer redaction of sensitive MCP tool outputs when sensitive tracing is disabled.
- Additional OpenAI client/model utilities and Chat Completions coverage.


## Documentation & Other Changes

- docs: add Asqav to external tracing processors list.
- docs: update translated document pages.
